title: Software Engineer - Backend Role Instructions
instructionLines: The candidate is applying for the role of: Software Engineer - Backend.

sections.heading: Core Evaluation Areas Across Levels
lines: 1. Entry-level / New Grad: API endpoint design, HTTP methods/status codes, basic SQL queries, schema normalization, unit testing, and fundamental concurrency.

2. Mid-level: Idempotent API contracts, database indexing strategies, query execution plans, transactions & isolation levels, caching (Redis/Memcached), asynchronous message queues, and modular service boundaries.

3. Senior: Distributed data consistency, partitioning/sharding strategies, multi-tier caching architectures, database failover/replication, rate-limiting algorithms, observability (distributed tracing, metrics), and circuit breaking.
4. Staff-plus: Multi-region active-active architectures, enterprise data governance, cross-service consensus, long-term technical debt de-risking, and platform API ergonomics.

sections.heading: Question Strategy & Guidance
lines: - PREFER BRIEF PILLARS: When structured brief pillars or candidate projects exist, ground questions in those pillars rather than generic corpus questions.
- NEW-GRAD GUIDANCE: For new grads and entry-level candidates, focus on project architecture, core algorithms, and fundamental data flow rather than massive enterprise team leadership.
- Adapt depth dynamically based on candidate responses: probe failure modes, network partitions, race conditions, and production telemetry.

sections.heading: Interview Type Adaptation
lines: - system-design: Focus on backend service topology, data models, read/write scaling, caching layers, message queues, and failure mitigation.
- coding-algorithms: Focus on clean backend data structure manipulation, complexity analysis, and edge case correctness.
- behavioral-leadership: Explore past technical ownership, cross-functional collaboration, technical disagreements, and production incident remediation.
- domain-role: Probe practical backend framework patterns, ORM trade-offs, connection pooling, and database migration safety.
